title: A Dog Ate John Hattie's Homework
author: Stephen Vainker
summary: Vainker documents institutional failure to investigate clear evidence of plagiarism, hallucinated citations, and AI-writing in prominent education pundit John Hattie's work. Despite hundreds of examples of plagiarism and fabricated references across four publications, institutions have refused accountability—the University of Melbourne claimed resource constraints and checked only 14 instances. The case reveals a crisis: when institutions benefit from a figure's profile, accountability becomes optional. Vainker asks whether elite institutions actually care about integrity when it costs them, and what hope remains for research-based education if supposed guardians prove indifferent to fraud.
points: Hattie has plagiarized across his PhD and publications while generating hallucinated citations in four publications where he is sole or lead author.
University of Melbourne and publishers refused meaningful investigation despite clear evidence presented.
Academic institutions profit from Hattie's profile while using that same profile to justify refusing accountability.
If elite institutions prove indifferent when fraud costs them, what incentive exists for downstream researchers to maintain standards?
The gatekeeping problem reveals itself: those claiming to guard scholarship ignore violations by high-profile figures.
quotes: There is scarcely a clearer case of failings of academic integrity.

The university and publishers calculated that their interests were best served in whitewashing Hattie's work.” “Do the highly-respected institutions that position themselves as guardians of true scholarship really have any interest in academic integrity when push comes to shove?” Archived from Stephen Vainker Substack on April 21, 2026 by Tim.
